question.text: This Canadian province held sovereignty referendums in 1980 and 1995 because many of its residents want to become an independent country. Unlike residents in other provinces, most of its residents speak French.
question.clue: The Meech Lake Accords were attempts to convince it to endorse the 1982 Constitution Act, and the Quiet Revolution occurred in this province.

swap.text: This province is the most populous and borders both Minnesota and New York. The capital Ottawa and the major city of Toronto both lie in this province.
swap.clue: The First Nations leader Tecumseh was killed in this province during the Battle of the Thames (TIMS) in the War of 1812.

question.leadin: The sign language used by this group is considered severely endangered, with less than forty native speakers worldwide.
question.text: Name this ethnic group that is indigenous to the arctic regions of Greenland and North America. They are known for their use of kayaks and dog sleds in transportation and hunting.
question.clue: In the 1950s, this ethnic group's dogs were killed by the RCMP.

swap.text: A Quebecois ["que-beck-WAA"] prime minister of Canada with this last name invoked the War Measures Act for the third time in history to end the October Crisis. His son with this surname won a third term as Canadian prime minister in 2021 federal elections.
swap.answerHtml: Trudeau [accept Pierre Trudeau or Joseph Philippe Pierre Yves Elliot Trudeau or Justin Trudeau or Justin Pierre James Trudeau]
swap.clue: Another politician with this name initiated the Phoenix Pay system, and was given the nickname "little potato" when attending a G20 summit in China.

question.leadin: This man's namesake "mania" followed his ascension to the head of the Liberal Party.
question.text: Name this man whose government enacted a Charter of Rights and Freedoms. He proclaimed "just watch me" three days before suspending the writ of habeas corpus under the War Measures Act.
question.clue: This co-founder and editor of Cite Libre also founded the Rassemblement Movement to reunite his country's political left and as Minister of Justice reformed his country's Criminal Code to elaborate on homosexuals, divorce, and abortion.

swap.leadin: This city donates a Christmas tree to Boston each year as thanks for aid following a major disaster.
swap.text: Name this city whose harbor experienced a massive explosion after the SS Mont-Blanc and the SS Imo collided in 1917.
swap.clue: During the French and Indian War, the British army kept prisoners on Georges Island in this city's harbor.

question.text: The Iroquois defeated the Huron in this series of wars sparked by competition for the fur of a certain animal. These wars ended with the signing of the Great Peace of Montreal.
question.clue: The Haudenosaunee fought these conflicts against the French and the Huron to gain control over the fur trade.

swap.leadin: Accusations of vote-buying in this scandal led to the swift introduction of a secret ballot by the next government.
swap.text: Name this scandal in which Hugh Allan bribed lawmakers to win a contract to build a railroad. It led to the downfall of John Macdonald's government.
swap.clue: Shortly after this event, secret ballots were introduced and Sandford Fleming was appointed by the Department of Public Works to ensure that certain parts of an enterprise were built publicly.

question.text: He kept appointed governor William McDougall from entering the Red River settlement and won favorable terms in the Manitoba Act. For 15 points, name this leader of the Metis who led a revolt of French-speaking Indian descendants against Canadian rule.
question.clue: This man's military general Gabriel Dumont was victorious at the Battle of Duck Lake, and he was forced into capture following defeat at the Battle of Batoche.

swap.text: After De Gaulle blurted out "Vive le Quebec libre!" at Montreal's Expo 67, this Nobel-winning Liberal Canadian Prime Minister responded, "Canadians do not need to be liberated."
swap.clue: This politician claimed "Canadians do not need to be liberated" in response to the "Vive le Quebec Libre" speech another man gave at Expo 67.

question.leadin: Name these explorers of the New World.
question.text: This French dude was the first explorer of the Gulf of St. Lawrence and discoverer of the St. Lawrence river.
question.clue: On their second voyage, this person made contact with the residents of the village of Stadacona.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about western exploration and settlement in America.
swap.text: It's unclear how many people actually drowned fording a river while traveling on the real-life Oregon Trail, but it is clear that the most famous Oregon Trail route began in this Missouri city, which was also the hometown of Harry Truman.

question.leadin: This organization kidnapped James Cross and killed Pierre Laporte.
question.text: Name this organization whose actions led to the October Crisis.
question.answerHtml: Front de libération du Québec (or FLQ, or Felquistes, or Quebec Liberation Front)
question.clue: Members of this group kidnapped British Trade Commissioner James Cross and Minister of Labour and Immigration Pierre Laporte.

swap.text: Canadian infantry troops under Julian Byng stormed Hill 145 at this World War I battle, losing thousands of men but earning respect from the British as a fighting force.
swap.answerHtml: Battle of Vimy Ridge [prompt on the Battle of Arras]
swap.clue: This battle began on Easter Monday 1917 as part of the Second Battle of Arras.

question.leadin: These people may have inspired the tuniit("toon-EAT"), a race of giants in a successor culture's mythology.
question.text: Name this archaeological culture, which preceded the Thule people in northern Canada and Greenland. Bows and arrows are conspicuously absent from their sites despite their use by the previous Saqqaq ("sah-KAHK") culture.
question.clue: X-shaped incisions on figures' heads from this culture have been linked to shamanistic travels.

swap.leadin: This alliance was first established through the efforts of the prophet known as the Great Peacemaker.
swap.text: The Great Peacemaker and his follower, Hiawatha, are considered to be the founders of this collective, also known as "The Great League of Peace," which the Tuscarora joined in 1722.
swap.answerHtml: Iroquois Confederacy/League [or Haudenosaunee; or or Six Nations; or Five Nations]
swap.clue: They also took the British side in the French and Indian War.

question.text: Wilfrid Laurier ("LORR-ee-ay") became Prime Minister after the Manitoba Schools crisis. His Minister of the Interior, Clifford Sifton, ran a hugely successful immigration campaign by marketing Canada's prairies with this three-word slogan.

swap.leadin: This man surrendered at the battle of Batoche.
swap.text: Name this man who initiated a failed 1885 uprising in Saskatchewan, but was eventually captured and hung. He had previously led an uprising in Manitoba called the Red River Rebellion.
swap.clue: A so-called "peace mission" under Garnet Wolseley forced him into exile after he was villified for insisting upon the execution of Thomas Scott.

question.leadin: This man worked with the Baring Brothers to secure financial backing for a railroad that connected Halifax to Windsor.
question.text: Name this publisher of the Novascotian and Morning Chronicle who accused local politicians of stealing over 30,000 pounds from the public treasury, then was acquitted in a landmark 1835 trial affirming the freedom of the press in Canada.

swap.text: This Canadian Prime Minister attended the joint funeral for nine of the women killed in the massacre. This man met with Ronald Reagan at the infamous "Shamrock Summit."
swap.clue: His government accepted refugees from the pro-American governments in Guatamala and El Salvador and engineered a failed agreement in Charlottetown that was to replace the Meech Lake Accord.
